one_liner: Teaches yoga, and at the therapy levels works with illness alongside doctors.
job_roles: Yoga Instructor | Yoga Wellness Instructor | Yoga Teacher & Evaluator | Assistant Yoga Therapist | Yoga Therapist | School Yoga Teacher | Corporate Yoga Instructor | Yoga Studio Instructor | Online Yoga Coach
self_emp_route: Own classes, studio or online practice. Almost all yoga teaching income in India is self-employed - group classes, personal clients, corporate contracts and retreats - and the overseas market pays several times Indian rates.
ai_reason: Low exposure. Adjusting a body in a room, judging what a person with a bad back should not do, and holding a group through a practice are physical and relational. Online Yoga Coach is the exposed role and it is exposed to free video rather than to AI - the internet is full of yoga instruction and always has been. Yoga Therapist is the most protected: it works with pathology alongside clinicians, and the YCB ladder is what certifies that.
role_spread: [Yoga Therapist, Assistant Yoga Therapist] higher: reasoning, conscientiousness, emotional_intelligence / lower: extraversion || [Online Yoga Coach, Corporate Yoga Instructor] higher: verbal, confidence, extraversion / lower: bodily || [School Yoga Teacher] higher: agreeableness, conscientiousness / lower: openness
path_to_entry: class_11_12: Any stream, or none for the entry YCB levels. A BA or MA in Yoga exists and is not required. -> training: A YCB-aligned course, or training at a recognised yoga institution. Practice depth matters more than course length. -> certification: YCB level certification - Protocol Instructor, then Wellness Instructor, then Teacher and Evaluator. Valid five years and renewable. -> specialisation: The therapy ladder - Assistant Yoga Therapist then Yoga Therapist - which is what opens hospital, AYUSH and clinical work and is where the pay separates.
nuances: [licensing_body] Null, and the distinction is commercially important rather than legal. YCB certification under the Ministry of AYUSH is a voluntary standardisation scheme - no statute bars an uncertified person from teaching yoga and nobody is struck off. What it does is open employment: government, schools, hospitals and reputable studios ask for it. || [demand_signal] High, and it is one of very few Indian professions with a genuine global market where India is the recognised source. That is why pathway is 'any': an Indian yoga teacher abroad earns several times the domestic rate, and it is a common career plan rather than an exception. || [economics] The employed figure describes a studio or gym instructor on a salary, which is a minority of this profession. Income here is per class, per client and per retreat, and a teacher with a full personal roster or an overseas base earns well above the range shown.

one_liner: Does skin, nails, hair removal and grooming treatments - salons, homes, bridal work.
job_roles: Beautician | Cosmetologist | Skin Care Therapist | Nail Technician | Threading & Waxing Specialist | Mehndi Artist | Bridal Beauty Specialist | Salon Receptionist & Coordinator | Home Service Beautician
self_emp_route: Own salon, or home service and bridal work taken directly. Capital for a small salon is modest and bridal season income is concentrated and high. This is the normal shape of the profession, not an alternative to it.
ai_reason: Almost unexposed. Every treatment here is hands on another person's skin, hair or nails, in a room, with the client present. What AI touches is the surrounding business - booking, recommendations, before-and-after imagery for marketing - and Salon Receptionist & Coordinator is the only role with meaningful exposure, through app-based booking that has already removed a good deal of front-desk work.
role_spread: [Bridal Beauty Specialist, Mehndi Artist] higher: openness, extraversion, bodily, emotional_stability / lower: - || [Home Service Beautician] higher: conscientiousness, extraversion, bodily / lower: confidence || [Salon Receptionist & Coordinator] higher: verbal, conscientiousness, extraversion / lower: bodily
path_to_entry: class_11_12: None. Class 8 or 10 is typical and many enter younger. -> training: A beauty and wellness course - BWSSC/NSQF aligned, a private academy, or apprenticeship in a salon. None is legally required. -> work: Salon assistant, then therapist. Entry pay is low and much of it is commission on treatments and product sales. -> independence: Own salon, home service practice, or bridal work - which is where the income actually changes and where most of this profession ends up.
review_reason: No sourced wage figure for Indian salon staff, and more importantly no figure for bridal or home-service earnings, which are where most of the income in this profession sits. At 4.2 LPA employed with independence named as the normal path and no ceiling, the record reads as a dead end for one of the largest occupations open to Indian women without qualifications.
nuances: [economics] Fails the compensation filter on the employed figure, which describes a salaried salon therapist - and that is not where this profession's money is. Bridal and home-service work is seasonal, cash and considerably better paid, and a salon owner is running a small business. The employed number is the floor, not the profession. || [demand_signal] High and among the most geographically distributed in the dataset - every town has salons, and the sector is one of the largest employers of Indian women without formal qualifications. App-based home service has extended it further into smaller cities. || [licensing_body] Null, and worth stating because these are invasive procedures. Anyone in India may perform chemical peels, bleaching and hair removal on a stranger with no training and no register. Certification is a private market with no floor, exactly as with Fitness Trainer in Sector 11.

one_liner: Cuts, colours and styles hair - salons, barbershops, homes, film and fashion.
job_roles: Hair Stylist | Barber | Hair Colourist | Salon Hair Technician | Bridal Hair Stylist | Hair Spa & Treatment Specialist | Session Stylist (Fashion & Film) | Trichology Assistant | Mobile Barber
self_emp_route: Own barbershop or salon chair, or freelance bridal and session work. A barbershop needs very little capital and is one of the most accessible small businesses in India; session styling needs a portfolio and a metro base.
ai_reason: Among the least exposed professions in the dataset. Cutting hair is manual skill performed on a specific head, in person, with an irreversible result. There is no digital output to substitute for and no plausible automation. The only role with any exposure is Trichology Assistant, through image-based scalp and hair analysis, which is a tool rather than a replacement.

nuances: [economics] The employed figure describes a salaried salon employee. The trade's normal form is a chair of your own - either renting one or running a shop - and a barber with a steady neighbourhood clientele or a stylist with bridal bookings earns well above the range shown. Session styling for fashion and film is a different economy again. || [demand_signal] High, universal and structurally safe. Hair grows everywhere, at the same rate, in every town, regardless of the economy. Along with tailoring it is one of the most reliably local livelihoods in this dataset.

one_liner: Paints faces for cameras, weddings and stages - and makes them survive lights and hours.

self_emp_route: Freelance bridal, film and fashion work booked directly or through agencies. This profession is essentially entirely self-employed, and bridal season is where the income is concentrated.
ai_reason: Low exposure. Makeup is applied by hand to a specific face and must survive hours and lights. Digital retouching has been available for two decades and did not remove the job, because the photograph is not the only deliverable - the person has to walk around looking like that. Makeup Retail Consultant carries the exposure, through virtual try-on tools that have already changed beauty retail.

one_liner: Gives therapeutic and relaxation treatments - spas, hotels, wellness centres, homes.
job_roles: Spa Therapist | Massage Therapist | Reflexologist | Aromatherapist | Hydrotherapy & Body Treatment Therapist | Spa Receptionist & Coordinator | Wellness Centre Supervisor | Visually Impaired Massage Therapist | Panchakarma Therapist | Ayurveda Therapist | Abhyanga & Oil Therapy Technician | Wellness Retreat Therapist
entrance_exams: Private spa and massage academy certifications
self_emp_route: Home-visit practice and independent clients, which is common and better paid than salon employment. Hotel and cruise ship contracts are the other route and pay considerably more.
ai_reason: Almost unexposed. Manual therapy is hands on a body reading tension and responding to it, and no part of that is digital. Massage devices and chairs exist and have existed for decades without displacing therapists, because the judgment about pressure and contraindication is the service. Spa Receptionist & Coordinator carries the only real exposure through booking automation.

path_to_entry: class_11_12: None. Class 10 is typical. -> training: A spa therapy or massage course - BWSSC/NSQF aligned, a hotel spa academy, or a specialist programme. Anatomy and contraindications are the parts that matter. -> work: Hotel spa, standalone spa or wellness centre, cruise ship, or home service. -> specialisation: A modality, or supervision. nuances: [job_roles] AYURVEDA & PANCHAKARMA THERAPIST WAS BUILT AS A SEPARATE PROFESSION AND MERGED IN ON REVIEW, on the Solar Panel Technician precedent in DECISIONS.md 8.95 - same object of concern, same skill set plus a specialisation. The evidence was that the two records came out numerically identical on every economic field: cost 1.0, early 1.5-3.6, mid 2.7-7.0, midpoint 4.85, payback 0.39, certificate tier, two years, open entry. Two professions a builder cannot tell apart will always surface together in a psychometric recommender, which is the noise the merge test exists to prevent. || [path_to_entry] One distinction survives the merge and must not be lost: a panchakarma THERAPIST is not an Ayurveda DOCTOR. Ayurveda Doctor in Sector 4 is a five-and-a-half-year BAMS with statutory registration and the right to diagnose and prescribe; the therapist performs treatments under that prescription. Marketing routinely conflates the two, which is how unqualified people come to present as Ayurvedic physicians. || [licensing_body] Null, and this profession needs the point made more sharply than most. Nothing in India registers a massage therapist or sets a standard for training in anatomy and contraindications, and the absence of regulation also leaves practitioners - who are disproportionately women and migrants working in private rooms - without a professional standing that would protect them. It is a safety gap in both directions. || [demand_signal] Moderate and split by segment. Hotel and wellness-tourism spa work is growing and pays reasonably; the standalone and home-service market is crowded and informal. Cruise ship and overseas contracts are the highest-paying route and are why pathway is 'any'.

one_liner: Makes permanent marks on people - tattooing, piercing, and the hygiene that must go with it.
job_roles: Tattoo Artist | Body Piercer | Permanent Makeup Artist | Tattoo Removal Technician | Scalp Micropigmentation Technician | Studio Hygiene & Sterilisation Technician | Tattoo Design Artist
self_emp_route: Own studio or a rented chair. This is the normal form of the profession and the artist's own following is the entire business.
ai_reason: Low exposure with one real crack. Tattoo Design Artist is directly exposed - generating tattoo designs is exactly what image models do, and clients now arrive with generated references. But the application is manual work on living skin with an irreversible result, and Tattoo Artist, Body Piercer and Permanent Makeup Artist are protected by that completely. What has changed is that the drawing is worth less and the hand is worth more.
role_spread: [Studio Hygiene & Sterilisation Technician] higher: conscientiousness, attention_span, logical / lower: openness || [Tattoo Design Artist] higher: openness, spatial, verbal / lower: bodily || [Permanent Makeup Artist, Scalp Micropigmentation Technician] higher: attention_span, spatial, conscientiousness / lower: openness
path_to_entry: class_11_12: None. Drawing ability matters and is not certified. -> training: Apprenticeship in a studio. There is no recognised Indian qualification, and courses sold as certification are not a substitute for supervised practice on skin. -> hygiene: Bloodborne pathogen and sterilisation training. This is the part that matters and nothing compels it. -> work: Studio artist, then your own studio or chair. Reputation is built on a public portfolio and healed work.
nuances: [profession] Routed here from Sector 8 and the decision is confirmed. The skill is drawing, which pointed at design - but the object of concern is a permanent, irreversible modification of a living person's body, governed by hygiene, consent and bloodborne infection risk. Those constraints belong to personal care, not to the design of objects. || [licensing_body] Null, and this is the most serious unregulated-practice gap in the sector. Tattooing and piercing break the skin and carry hepatitis and HIV transmission risk, and India has no national licensing, no mandatory sterilisation standard and no inspection regime for studios. A student entering this trade should understand that the hygiene discipline is entirely on them.
